lead: >-
  Paraguay has no coastline. The beach theme in Ada Tours' selection refers to a multi-country journey: a 16-day tour begins with time on the Atlantic coast in Punta del Este, Uruguay, continues to Paraguay for Asunción, the Chaco and Guairá, and ends at Iguazu Falls. The beach stops are in Uruguay, not Paraguay. Paraguay offers Lake Ypacaraí and sightseeing, but the program includes neither a seaside resort nor a promised swimming experience. Compare the days by country to choose the right trip without misplaced expectations.
---

## Are there beach holidays in Paraguay?

**Paraguay is landlocked.** A journey including Atlantic beaches can therefore be arranged only in combination with another country. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring both Paraguay and a beach element. Here, this means the [16-day itinerary through Uruguay, Paraguay, Brazil and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/).

Its beach days take place in **[Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) in Uruguay**; the Paraguayan portion focuses on towns, natural areas and culture. The beach theme applies to the entire tour, which is why it appears in the Paraguay selection as well. This does not mean there is a beach resort on Paraguayan territory.

| Days | Activities |
|---|---|
| 1–3, Uruguay | Cities and transfer to the ocean |
| 4–5, Uruguay | Punta del Este beaches |
| 6–12, Paraguay | Asunción, the Chaco and Guairá |
| 13–16 | Iguazu Falls and return journey |

The table distinguishes swimming from sightseeing at a glance. If you want to spend most of your holiday by the ocean, compare [Uruguay beach itineraries](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/uruguay/) and [Brazil beach itineraries](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/). If discovering Paraguay is your priority, explore the [complete Paraguay tours catalog](/paraguay/tour/) without a beach filter.

## Punta del Este: where the beaches are on this journey

The first part of the [16-day journey](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) takes place in Uruguay. Travelers begin with [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/), followed by wineries in Canelones. On day 3, the route reaches [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/), a town on the Atlantic coast.

### Day 4: Playa Mansa and Playa Brava

The itinerary describes two different shores of Punta del Este. **Playa Mansa** is more sheltered from open-ocean waves. Nearby are the harbor, marinas, restaurants and town facilities. **Playa Brava** faces the Atlantic and is more exposed to wind and surf. The famous La Mano sculpture is on this side.

The sightseeing day covers the town, marinas and the Casapueblo museum. You can experience both types of shore and the resort's architecture, but **day 4 is not described as an entire free day of swimming**: an individual sightseeing program is scheduled. When choosing a trip, distinguish a visit to a beach town from unstructured time beside the water.

### Day 5: free time by the ocean

The following day is set aside for leisure in Punta del Este. You can walk along Playa Mansa, spend time on the beach, choose a restaurant or explore the town streets. A return to Montevideo is planned for the evening. This is the clearest **free beach day** in the published program.

Two days in the resort area are not the same as a full week by the sea. The trip suits someone who wants to visit several countries and include a brief ocean break at the beginning. If the central goal of your vacation is swimming every day, you will need another route or a separately agreed change to the program.

## After the coast: Paraguay without a seaside resort

Day 6 features a flight to [Asunción](/paraguay/place/asuncion/), where the nature of the journey changes. Ocean beaches give way to historical excursions, journeys into the Chaco and visits to communities.

On day 8, the route goes into the [Chaco](/paraguay/place/chaco/) and [Filadelfia](/paraguay/place/filadelfia/), stopping at [Fortín Toledo](/paraguay/place/fortin-toledo-reserve/). Day 9 includes [Laguna Capitán](/paraguay/place/laguna-capitan/), where birdwatching is possible. On day 10, travelers meet an Indigenous community in the region before returning to Asunción.

This is a journey through dry natural areas and cultural sites. **The saline Laguna Capitán appears as a nature stop for observations, not an equipped bathing beach.** The presence of water in photographs should not change the meaning of the excursion.

If these natural stops are what appeal to you, [Paraguay nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/paraguay/) explain the time required for the Chaco and how lagoon visits are organized. For historical attractions, see [Paraguay cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/paraguay/).

## San Bernardino and Ypacaraí: a lake does not guarantee swimming

On day 11, travelers pass through [Areguá](/paraguay/place/aregua/) and [San Bernardino](/paraguay/place/san-bernardino/) beside Lake Ypacaraí, then continue to [Colonia Independencia](/paraguay/place/colonia-independencia/) and the [Ybytyruzú Mountains](/paraguay/place/ybytyruzu-mountain-range/).

San Bernardino has a history as a lakeside resort and places for strolling. Yet including the lake in the itinerary **does not confirm that swimming is included**. This day covers towns, mountain scenery, forest trails and waterfalls. The water is part of the landscape, not a promised beach product.

Water quality in Lake Ypacaraí deserves special attention. Paraguay's Ministry of the Environment has published monitoring results advising against swimming in certain shoreline areas. Those findings apply to particular dates, so any future trip requires current data, local restrictions and official advice. **Presenting Ypacaraí as a guaranteed swimming destination would be misleading.**

Some accommodation options in the Guairá region mention private swimming pools. This is a characteristic of certain lodging options, not a guarantee that every traveler will be assigned such accommodation. If a pool is essential, confirm it for the particular property.

## Iguazu: experiences beside water, but not beach time

On day 13, the group passes through [Ciudad del Este](/paraguay/place/ciudad-del-este/) to Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil. Visits follow to the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls, with excursions such as Macuco Safari and the Bird Park.

The falls are a major natural highlight, but they should not be counted as beach days. Walking along waterfall viewpoints or riding a boat near the cascades is different from relaxing on an ocean shore. Both the Brazilian side of Iguazu and Argentina's Devil's Throat are outside Paraguay, although they form part of the overall multi-country route.

If you like the idea of combining beaches with waterfalls, compare the allocation of days between the [Uruguayan ocean coast](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/uruguay/) and [multi-country sightseeing](/multi-country/). The itinerary description does not establish any additional opportunity to swim at the falls.

## When to travel for the ocean and how much time to allow

The Punta del Este itinerary identifies the Uruguayan summer—December, January and February—as the principal resort season. January is usually busier, while December and February may appeal to those seeking a less crowded town experience. March is presented as a quieter alternative. These are general seasonal guidelines from the itinerary, not guarantees of water temperature or weather on any particular date.

For a beach vacation, count **complete days beside the sea**, not the length of the whole tour. This route reaches Punta del Este on day 3, features sightseeing on day 4 and free time on day 5, followed by a return to Montevideo. The journey then moves to a different geographical setting.

When choosing dates, take account of both Uruguay's coastal weather and conditions on the Paraguayan road journeys. The Chaco climate differs from the coast, so clothing and plans for the two segments may differ. Comfortable shoes, sun protection and readiness for vehicle excursions are important in the Chaco; the Uruguayan coast calls for clothing suitable for wind, walks and beach time.

## Who should choose this itinerary—and who should look elsewhere?

The tour is for travelers who want to see Uruguay's Atlantic coast, discover Paraguay and finish at Iguazu. Beach time is an enjoyable opening to a longer trip rather than its sole purpose. History, nature and several countries occupy many more days than the beach.

If the sea is your main goal, our [entire beach holidays catalog](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/) offers a wider choice. For longer stays on the coast, look for routes with more genuinely free resort days, rather than relying on a beach-themed label.

If Paraguay is your main priority, a nature- or culture-focused itinerary makes more sense. You can add an ocean coast in a neighboring country as a separate segment if the new route and terms are agreed in advance. Do not assume such an extension is included in the original tour price.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does a beach tour appear in the Paraguay catalog?

Because the [16-day multi-country journey](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) includes both Paraguay and a substantial beach stop in Uruguay. The theme applies to the entire trip. This program's beaches are not in Paraguay.

### Does Paraguay have ocean beaches?

No. Paraguay has no ocean coast. Rivers and lakes may have beach areas, but these are different from seaside resorts and require separate checks of swimming safety.

### How many beach days are included?

Punta del Este has a sightseeing day on day 4 and free time on day 5; arrival in town is on day 3. Day 5 ends with the return to Montevideo. The tour does not include a full week of beach relaxation.

### Can visitors swim in Lake Ypacaraí?

The resort's name does not establish whether the water is currently safe for swimming. Paraguay's Environment Ministry has previously reported unsatisfactory water tests on certain lakeside beaches. Check new official data and local restrictions before any trip. Swimming in Ypacaraí is not included in the published itinerary.

### Are the Punta del Este beaches and Iguazu Falls in the same country?

No. Punta del Este is in Uruguay. The waterfalls on this itinerary are visited from Brazil and Argentina, with the Paraguay segment of the journey between them.

### Can I increase the number of days at the ocean?

You can discuss this when designing an individual route, but extra nights at the resort are not included in the currently published program. Their price, availability and changes to transport must be agreed separately.

lead: >-
  A beach holiday in Peru can be combined with Machu Picchu, Cusco and Lake Titicaca. But similarly named itineraries differ in where their seaside stays take place: one Ada Tours program ends on the Pacific coast of Tumbes, while another combines Peru with Brazil and reserves its Atlantic beach days for Búzios. Compare the location, number of free days and flights before choosing.
---

## Beach tours featuring Peru: where is the seaside stay?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both programs visit Peru's cultural regions, but **their beach stays take place in different countries**. If you want to finish your trip by swimming in the Pacific Ocean in Peru itself, choose the route through [Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/). If the goal is to combine Machu Picchu, Iguazu and Rio with Atlantic beaches, look at the journey through [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/).

| Itinerary | Beach segment |
|---|---|
| [Peru and Tumbes](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) | Punta Sal, Peru |
| [Peru and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) | Búzios, Brazil |

The important measure is not a tour's overall length but **how many full days remain at the coast after flights and transfers**. Arriving at a resort in the evening and traveling back to the airport do not usually count as full free days by the sea.

## The Pacific after the Andes: the Tumbes beaches itinerary

The [16-day Complete Peru + Tumbes Beaches tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) begins in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) and continues through [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). After [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), travelers visit [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). This is an intensive sightseeing segment involving cities, archaeology, highlands and transfers.

Day 12 includes a flight from Lima to Tumbes and a transfer to **Punta Sal**. **Days 13 and 14 are entirely free for relaxing beside the Pacific Ocean**: no compulsory excursions are planned, and full board is specified on both days. On day 15, travelers fly back to Lima, with departure planned for day 16. Full board relates to the named beach days; it must not automatically be assumed for every hotel on the route.

The northern coast works especially well as a peaceful ending to a substantial itinerary. After the altitudes of Cusco and Titicaca and the road journeys near Colca, the schedule becomes more relaxed. There is also an option to add [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) and Nazca; these are additional visits, not already included beach days.

### Tumbes, Punta Sal and Máncora: what is the difference?

[Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/) is a northern coastal region and city providing access to resorts. **Punta Sal** is known for long sandy beaches and a quieter style of vacation; this is where the transfer goes in the described itinerary. [Máncora](/peru/place/mancora/) is farther south and often appeals to surfers and travelers looking for restaurants and a livelier atmosphere. These resorts are not the same stop.

Máncora matters when choosing a Peruvian beach destination independently, but **it is not a scheduled stop** on Complete Peru + Tumbes Beaches. If you specifically want to stay in Máncora, discuss changes to the route and transfers separately; the fact that a destination is listed on the site does not mean it is included in your tour.

## Peru and Brazil: Machu Picchu and Atlantic beaches

On the [13-day Peru, Machu Picchu, Brazil and Rio itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/), the first part of the trip passes through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lake Titicaca. It then continues to Brazil: Iguazu Falls, [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/).

Day 11 is devoted to travel from Rio to Búzios and check-in. **Day 12 is free**: you can relax on the beach, choose water activities or take a boat trip. Day 13 includes the transfer for your return flight. Activities mentioned as possibilities, such as surfing and boat excursions, must not automatically be treated as services paid for by the tour.

This is a different kind of journey: see the sights of two countries and conclude beside the sea. The beach days are **in Brazil on the Atlantic Ocean**, so travelers who specifically want a Peruvian beach resort should choose the Tumbes itinerary. The combined route nevertheless offers Inca heritage and Brazilian landscapes in a single journey.

## When to plan a beach holiday in Peru

Peru's coastal climate varies markedly with latitude. In the far north around Tumbes, Punta Sal and Máncora, seawater is generally warmer than around Lima and farther south. **December to March** is the local summer and traditional beach season. It is a guideline for selecting dates, not a promise of uninterrupted sun or calm seas.

[Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) is a different type of destination, known for desert scenery, coastal cliffs and marine wildlife around the Ballestas Islands. Visits here commonly involve walks and marine excursions. **Paracas is not an equivalent replacement for several days at a Tumbes beach resort**, particularly when swimming and free time by the water are the main goals.

On a combined itinerary, the seasons in the Andes matter too. Conditions suitable for mountain excursions around Cusco do not always coincide with the warmest and sunniest coastal weather. Choose your dates according to your main priority: **Machu Picchu and sightseeing** or **several days beside a warm sea**. General information about the country's regions and routes appears in our [Peru guide](/peru/); here the focus is on comparing the actual beach stops on available trips.

## Choosing an itinerary without unnecessary transfers

For a stay entirely within Peru, choose the [Tumbes itinerary](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/): two full free days by the ocean follow an extensive sightseeing program. This tour includes domestic flights and highland regions, so if your vacation is short, decide in advance whether you want every stop before the beach.

If combining **two countries** is more important, the [Peru + Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) reaches the Brazilian coast via Iguazu and Rio. The published program includes less free time by the sea: one complete day in Búzios between arrival and departure. This appeals more to travelers who like combined itineraries and see the beach as a relaxing finale.

When comparing trips, also check exact flight days, confirmed meals and the option of adding excursions. **The label "beach tour" does not itself tell you how long you will spend on the beach or which services are included in the price.** Those differences appear in the individual itineraries and help you choose a comfortable pace.

## Frequently asked questions about beach tours in Peru

### Can I combine Machu Picchu with beaches in Peru without going to Brazil?

Yes. The [Peru tour with a Tumbes beach stay](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) includes Machu Picchu, other regions of Peru and a separate beach segment in Punta Sal. There is no need to cross a national border to reach the sea on this itinerary.

### How many free seaside days are included in the Tumbes program?

Two full days: days 13 and 14. Day 12 involves arrival and a transfer to the resort; day 15 is the return to Lima. Full board is specified for those two beach days in the published program.

### Are all the beaches in this selection located in Peru?

No. The [Peru + Brazil program](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) includes Peruvian cities and monuments, but its beach segment is in Búzios, Brazil. For seaside relaxation on the Peruvian coast itself, choose [Tumbes](/peru/place/tumbes/).

### When is Peru's northern coast warmer?

Usually from December to March, during the local summer. The northern resorts differ from the cooler central and southern coast. Consider the weather, sea conditions and plans for highland excursions together.

### Are surfing, boat trips and excursions included on beach days?

Only when explicitly listed as included in the conditions of the particular tour. In Búzios, these are mentioned as possible free-day activities, while the two complete days in Tumbes are reserved for relaxation without compulsory excursions. Check the exact services on the [Tumbes itinerary](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) or the [multi-country program](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/).

## Beach tours featuring Uruguay: where will you actually go to the sea?

Our catalog offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} connected with both beach holidays and Uruguay. **This does not mean the beaches are in Uruguay on every itinerary.** Uruguay may form part of the main route or be offered as an optional visit. For a trip specifically focused on the Uruguayan coast, choose one with [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) rather than simply looking for Uruguay in a long list of countries visited.

The two current journeys serve different purposes. The [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay itinerary](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) covers Montevideo, Colonia, wineries in Canelones and the resort town of Punta del Este, then continues to Paraguay and Iguazu. The [11-day Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) combines Patagonia and the waterfalls with time on Brazil's tropical coast. In the latter case, Montevideo is an optional excursion on a free day, and the ocean resort is in Brazil.

| Itinerary | Location of the beach stay |
|---|---|
| [Uruguay and Paraguay, 16 days](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) | Punta del Este, Uruguay |
| [Argentina and Brazil, 11 days](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) | Praia de Pipa, Brazil |

The durations include cities, nature, flights and road journeys, so they do not equal the number of days at the beach. Below, we compare the current terms without confusing prices for different room types and included services.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_tur_po_uruguayu_i_paragvayu_16_dnej,tour_argentina_brazil_pipa_11d}}

## Where to enjoy the Uruguayan coast on the 16-day tour

### Punta del Este: two sides of the peninsula

[Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) sits where the Río de la Plata estuary meets the Atlantic coast. The itinerary identifies Playa Mansa and Playa Brava. The first is better sheltered and is generally chosen for calmer time by the water. Playa Brava faces ocean waves and features the famous La Mano sculpture, an extensive sandy beach and lively sections of promenade.

This distinction is more useful than simply asking for the "best beaches in Uruguay." Those who enjoy walks beside an open ocean may prefer the atmosphere of Playa Brava; for calmer water, look first at sheltered areas of Playa Mansa. Even at a normally quiet beach, conditions vary with wind, swell and weather. For swimming, check designated areas and current lifeguard warnings.

The itinerary includes [Punta Ballena](/uruguay/place/punta-ballena/), Casapueblo and resort life in Punta del Este. Casapueblo is a distinctive white building above the coast, making it possible to combine beaches with architecture and bay views. Beach time can alternate with a walk around the marina, cafés and galleries. However, a particular restaurant or boat excursion is not automatically included simply because it is available at the resort.

### How much time is actually left by the sea?

The [Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/) begins in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and the country's historical regions, then travels via [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) to Punta del Este. There is a day devoted to the beaches, marina and Casapueblo, followed by a free day at the resort before returning to the capital. Travelers therefore have time not only to see the shore during sightseeing, but also to spend some hours on the beach independently.

The Uruguayan section is followed by Paraguay: Asunción, the Chaco, other natural and cultural areas, and finally Iguazu Falls. This suits travelers wanting to connect several countries and contrasting landscapes. For a week entirely beside the ocean, it would be too sightseeing-intensive: most of the 16 days are spent elsewhere.

It is also useful to distinguish time **at the resort** from time **on the sand**. A transfer, checking in, sightseeing and a winery visit may all occupy parts of one calendar day. For a genuinely unhurried holiday, count the free days without mandatory outings.

## The second tour: Brazilian beaches and optional Uruguay

The [11-day Argentina and Brazil program](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) begins in Buenos Aires, then visits Patagonia's glacier region and Iguazu Falls. The final days are spent in [Praia de Pipa](/brazil/place/praia-de-pipa/) on Brazil's northeastern coast. Sandy beaches, cliffs, palm trees and a warm tropical coastline are the main attractions. The itinerary describes free time for swimming, relaxing and strolling.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is mentioned as a possible additional outing from Buenos Aires. There are no nights on Uruguayan beaches in the main route. It would be misleading to describe this tour as a Punta del Este vacation or transfer its beach conditions from Praia de Pipa to Uruguay.

When choosing between the journeys, consider one question: **do you want to swim specifically in Uruguay?** If yes, the first itinerary is a better match. If you prefer a beach break after Patagonia and Iguazu, and Uruguay appeals only as an opportunity to see another capital, the second is designed for that purpose. Other itineraries with seaside stops in neighboring countries are available under [beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/).

## How Uruguay's coast differs from other beach destinations

### The Uruguayan summer and travel season

Uruguay is in the Southern Hemisphere, where the busiest summer tourism period falls in December, January and February. Popular resorts attract the most visitors then, and nightlife in Punta del Este is more noticeable. January is an especially common choice for a beach trip. Seasonal warmth, however, does not guarantee identical water temperatures, calm waves or windless weather.

Outside the peak season, the coast is better suited to walks and exploring towns than guaranteed swimming. Conditions depend on the beach and the forecast. If the sea is your principal reason for traveling to Uruguay, the season matters more than a generic promise of "South America all year round."

When comparing [Uruguay tours](/uruguay/tour/) with visits to tropical Brazil, account for differences in climate and distance. The beaches of Punta del Este and Praia de Pipa are far apart and involve completely different routes. You cannot assume that water temperature or swimming conditions at one resort apply to the other.

### Two other areas for a separate beach itinerary

[Piriápolis](/uruguay/place/piriapolis/) combines a seafront promenade, coastal walks and outings into the nearby hills. It has a less urban resort atmosphere than Punta del Este. Neither of the two tours being compared includes a separate stay here, so it is an idea for another journey, not an unmentioned part of the current offer.

Farther east is Rocha department and the resort of La Paloma. According to the regional tourism authority, its beaches have different wave conditions, with both sheltered sections and more exposed surfing spots. La Paloma appeals to travelers who like smaller coastal towns, but it is not on either of the two itineraries. Mentioning the Rocha coast does not establish that Ada Tours offers a ready-made excursion there.

For an introduction to the country's geography, towns and natural attractions, see our [Uruguay guide](/uruguay/). If wineries and local cuisine are your main goals, explore [Uruguay food and wine itineraries](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/), where visits to producers are confirmed in individual tours.

## Choosing beach days and planning logistics

**First check three details of the actual program:** which beach is named, how much time is free of mandatory excursions and what onward transport is required. In Uruguay, major resorts combine readily with Montevideo and wine-growing areas, but visiting a new stretch of coastline takes time. On a long multi-country trip, too many transfers can leave fewer hours beside the sea than the tour's name suggests.

Second, separate included services from activities available during free time. Beach time usually lets you choose a restaurant, walk or place to relax, but does not mean sun loungers, water excursions or a specific beachfront hotel are included. Read those terms on the chosen tour page; benefits of one offer should not be assumed for another.

Third, if Uruguay is an optional stop, consider the departure city. An additional one-day trip from Buenos Aires focuses on Montevideo, not on a full vacation at Atlantic beaches. A proper beach trip within Uruguay needs separate nights on the coast.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which Ada Tours itineraries actually include a Uruguayan beach stay?

In this selection, the beach stay in Uruguay is confirmed on the [16-day Uruguay and Paraguay tour](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/). It includes a stop at Punta del Este and free time there. The [11-day Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) ends its beach segment in Brazil.

### Where is the water calmer: Playa Mansa or Playa Brava?

Playa Mansa is better sheltered, while Playa Brava faces ocean waves. Actual swimming conditions still depend on wind and sea state, so follow local warnings even on the calmer shoreline.

### When is the best time for Uruguay's beaches?

December through February is the usual choice for a classic summer holiday. January is generally busier. Other months can suit walks and sightseeing, but weather and water temperatures are less predictable for swimming.

### Can beaches be combined with wineries?

Yes. On the [16-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/uruguay-paraguay-16-days-2026/), a wine-tasting visit to [Canelones](/uruguay/place/canelones/) precedes Punta del Este. For a trip more focused on wine, compare [dedicated food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/uruguay/).

### Is an outing from Buenos Aires enough for a beach holiday in Uruguay?

No. The usual optional excursion from Buenos Aires covers Montevideo. Punta del Este's Atlantic beaches require separate time and transport. If the beach is essential, choose an itinerary with a resort stop and free days.

  Beach tours in Venezuela differ mainly in where and for how long travelers stay beside the Caribbean Sea. Margarita Island offers several days in an all-inclusive resort, the Los Roques archipelago offers small islands reached by boat, and Choroní combines beaches with Henri Pittier National Park. On our itineraries, the seaside segment ranges from a few stops to several free days and often accompanies a trip to Angel Falls. Compare actual days at the water, flights and included excursions.
---

## Beach tours in Venezuela: Los Roques, Margarita or Choroní?

**If you want several restful days by the sea in a single hotel, start with programs visiting [Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/). If white-sand islands and boat trips appeal to you, choose [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/). For a mix of beaches and wooded mountains, consider [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/).** These are three different approaches to a Caribbean vacation.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a beach segment in Venezuela. Most of these trips also visit cities, national parks or remote natural areas. Consequently, the total duration and the actual number of beach days can differ considerably. A 12-day journey, for example, might include four free days by the sea—or only a short island stop before flying to Bolivia.

This page helps you choose **a specific program with time on the coast**. For the country's overall geography and seasons, see our [Venezuela guide](/venezuela/); compare different countries and styles of seaside travel under [Latin American beach holidays](/interests/beach-holidays/).

## Six programs: how much time is spent on the beach?

| Tour | Seaside stay |
|---|---|
| [Margarita after Canaima](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) | 4 free days at the hotel |
| [Popular Destinations of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) | Margarita and an island excursion |
| [Tropical Contrasts](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) | Los Roques and Margarita |
| [Venezuela and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) | 2 days in Los Roques |

The number of seaside days is taken from the current itineraries. Flying to or leaving an island does not constitute a full free beach day. Los Roques programs require flights, and excursions to more distant islets may be offered at additional cost.

For a longer stay at one resort, start by comparing the two Margarita tours. For different marine landscapes in one trip, Tropical Contrasts is particularly interesting. Choose Choroní for the mainland Caribbean coast, small bays and nearby forests.

## Margarita: more free days and a resort-style vacation

[Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) lies in the Caribbean Sea off northeastern Venezuela. It has seaside communities, hotels, beaches with varying swimming conditions, historic towns and forts. A Margarita holiday can be based at a single hotel, with sightseeing arranged on separate days.

Notable coastal areas include Playa El Agua and El Yaque. They have distinct characteristics and water conditions; choose your hotel based on its particular beach, not merely the island's name. **A tour mentioning Margarita does not necessarily visit all its famous beaches.**

### When the itinerary really includes four free beach days

The [12-day Best of Venezuela tour with Margarita](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) follows [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/) and [Canaima with Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) with a flight via Caracas to Margarita. The beach segment begins with check-in at Sunsol Ecoland on an all-inclusive basis. **Four consecutive days** are then reserved for relaxing by the sea. An island sightseeing excursion is available on request but is listed as optional.

This option suits travelers who first want to experience Venezuela's famous natural sights and then spend several days without compulsory excursions. Keep in mind that the flight day from Canaima includes a connection and hotel transfer, so relaxation begins only after the journey. Confirm the exact meals and drinks included under the chosen accommodation and tour conditions.

### When the Margarita sightseeing excursion is already scheduled

The [Popular Destinations of Venezuela tour](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) also combines Caracas, Canaima and Margarita, but the island segment is arranged differently. After a flight and check-in at a 4-star all-inclusive hotel, travelers have free beach days and a separate island sightseeing tour.

The excursion day includes Juan Griego, La Galera Fortress, La Asunción, the Pampatar area and other island locations. It reveals local history and life, but **is no longer a full day of uninterrupted beach relaxation**. Further time by the sea follows later in the program.

If maximum free time with minimal compulsory transfers is your goal, begin with the [four-free-day itinerary](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/). If you would also like to explore the island, compare [Popular Destinations](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/).

## Los Roques: small islands, boats and white sand

The [Los Roques archipelago](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) is a Caribbean national park with numerous small islands, coral reefs and sandbars. According to Venezuela's Ministry of Tourism, Gran Roque is the archipelago's inhabited center. Reaching beaches on other islands involves boat travel. Snorkeling, birdwatching and relaxing on the shore are possible in designated areas of the protected waters.

What matters most to visitors here is **not so much a hotel category or large resort infrastructure as the particular island of the day, the boat crossing and sea conditions**. Los Roques offers a different experience from four consecutive days at one resort hotel on Margarita.

### On the two-day program: Madrisquí or Francisquí

On the [12-day Tropical Contrasts tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), day 2 starts with a flight from Caracas to Los Roques. Under the current program, relaxation takes place on Madrisquí or Francisquí, with a sun lounger and a packed lunch with drinks provided. The next day also features the islands, after which the group flies back to Caracas in the afternoon.

**Cayo de Agua, distant islands, a visit to the sea turtle conservation station and fishing are listed as optional opportunities.** They must not be presented as guaranteed stops on the core itinerary. Admission to Los Roques National Park is not included separately in the tour price; the current fee and conditions need to be checked when arranging the trip.

The tour continues to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and the [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/), then reaches Margarita for several additional all-inclusive relaxation days. For travelers who want to experience **two types of Caribbean coast** on one journey, this is more varied than programs with only one resort.

### Los Roques as a short seaside segment before Bolivia

The [12-day Venezuela and Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) also devotes **two days to Los Roques**. It includes a flight, time on Madrisquí or Francisquí, packed lunches with drinks and a return flight to Caracas. After Canaima, the journey continues into [Bolivia](/bolivia/): via La Paz to the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and Altiplano lagoons.

This is for travelers who want the Caribbean Sea to be a vivid but relatively brief part of a larger nature journey. There are no extra Margarita beach days on this itinerary. One important detail: **continental flights, including Caracas–La Paz–Caracas, are listed separately among the exclusions**, so prices cannot be compared directly with Venezuela-only tours without accounting for airfare.

## Choroní: mainland beaches and Henri Pittier National Park

[Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/) is on the Caribbean coast of Aragua state beside the wooded slopes of Henri Pittier National Park. It suits travelers interested in small seaside settlements, beaches tucked into bays and short walks through tropical vegetation.

Venezuela's national parks administration identifies Playa Grande near Choroní, Cata Bay and Cuyagua, a popular surfing spot, among the region's well-known beaches. **Some stretches have powerful surf**, so check swimming conditions at the specific beach. Being on the Caribbean coast does not mean every section is safe for children or calm swimming.

### New Conquistadors: one free day and optional boat outings

On the [New Conquistadors itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), the journey begins with a transfer from Caracas to Choroní and check-in at a small posada. The following day is left free for relaxation. Boat excursions to neighboring beaches, including Chuao, Cuyagua and other bays, are described as **optional**.

This offers a blend of the coast, a historic village and insights into cocoa-growing culture. But a list of possible beaches does not mean they are all visited in one day or prepaid. After Choroní, the itinerary continues to Canaima, then the Los Llanos savannas and the Venezuelan Andes.

### Nature and Beaches: Choroní before a long nature itinerary

On another [12-day tour combining beaches and ecotourism](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), Choroní occupies the opening days. Day 1 includes the transfer, accommodation at a posada, meals and optional trips to beaches; day 2 is reserved for relaxation and possible local outings. The journey then continues to [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/), mountain regions and [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/).

The difference from New Conquistadors goes beyond the beaches bearing similar names. The itineraries differ in guiding, later destinations and included services. Compare the **complete route after day 3**, not only the first two days by the sea.

## How the beaches connect with Angel Falls

Almost every seaside option described here also includes time in natural regions. [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) require their own segment involving flights, river journeys and a hike to a viewpoint. Some itineraries offer a different format of visiting the falls when water levels are low. Our [Venezuela guide](/venezuela/) explains the background, while individual tour pages specify the actual conditions.

**Consider the beach portion separately from days in Canaima.** Swimming near a waterfall and taking a lagoon boat excursion are nature activities, not substitutes for an unhurried day beside the Caribbean Sea. On a short vacation, decide what matters most: more free days on Margarita, boat outings around Los Roques or nature routes after Choroní.

Another combination of nature and beaches is [Tropical Contrasts](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), with Canaima and the Orinoco Delta between Los Roques and Margarita. [Venezuela–Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) is suitable for those who want to see the highlands of South America after their Caribbean visit.

## What to check before choosing a beach tour

### Free days and travel days

Domestic flights, connections through Caracas and transfers to hotels may take up substantial parts of a day. The [Margarita tour with four free days](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) allocates a separate day to arrival on the island. On Los Roques trips, the second of two island days ends with a flight back. It is therefore more useful to examine each day's activities than divide a tour's overall duration by the number of resorts.

### "All-inclusive" applies to specific accommodation

Hotels on Margarita are explicitly described as all-inclusive on several trips. This relates to the island stay and **does not automatically extend to Caracas, Canaima, Los Roques or Choroní**. Los Roques programs separately mention packed lunches and drinks on beach days; in nature areas, meals are listed by itinerary.

Included excursions, Russian-speaking guiding, international flights, park fees and alcohol also differ. For example, the [Popular Destinations tour](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) already schedules the Margarita sightseeing excursion, while [Best of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) lists it as an extra. Before choosing, read the "Included" and "Not Included" sections of the particular program.

### Season, wind and sea conditions

The [Venezuela guide](/venezuela/) describes a dry period roughly from December to April and a rainy season from May to November. Weather and sea conditions vary, however, among islands, mainland coastline and inland tropical regions. Even during drier months, there may be waves, strong winds or a postponed boat outing.

Los Roques is a protected marine area, so conservation restrictions apply to particular islands and activities. Boat availability and access to beaches should be agreed when planning the trip. On Margarita, select accommodation with the shore and activities in mind: calm swimming, long walks and water sports call for different conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about beach tours in Venezuela

### For four days without compulsory excursions, should I choose Margarita or Los Roques?

On Ada Tours' current itineraries, **four free days at a hotel are explicitly scheduled on Margarita** on the [Best of Venezuela tour](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/). Los Roques occupies two days on the relevant combined programs, one of which ends with the return flight. Compare Margarita itineraries for an extended resort stay.

### Is there a tour including both Los Roques and Margarita?

Yes. [Tropical Contrasts](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) visits Los Roques first, then Canaima and the Orinoco Delta, before several days on Margarita. The two seaside segments are separated by substantial travel and nature excursions; it is an active journey rather than an uninterrupted beach vacation.

### Can a Venezuelan beach vacation be combined with Bolivia?

Yes. The [12-day Venezuela and Bolivia journey](/multi-country/tour/venezuela-bolivia-nature-culture-12-days/) begins in Los Roques, then travels to Canaima and Bolivia, including Uyuni. The sea segment lasts two days. Take account of the separately listed international flight conditions.

### Are all boat excursions around Los Roques included?

No. On [Tropical Contrasts](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), the main visit to Madrisquí or Francisquí is specified, while farther islands and some additional activities are optional. Individual boat outings depend on the itinerary and local conditions.

### Where can I combine beaches and tropical forests without an island flight?

Consider [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/). On [New Conquistadors](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) and [Nature and Beaches](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), the opening days follow the mainland coastline near Henri Pittier National Park. The programs then visit different parts of Venezuela.

### Is every Venezuelan beach suitable for calm swimming?

No. Waves, depth and access differ from place to place. On Margarita, check the precise hotel location; on Los Roques, the selected island and boat conditions; at Choroní, the surf at the particular bay. This is especially important when traveling with children.

Choose the seaside segment you genuinely want, then compare flights, mandatory excursions and free days. For a substantial sightseeing journey, start with the [Venezuela tours catalog](/venezuela/tour/). If the beach is your deciding criterion, begin with the [beach holidays selection](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/venezuela/) and open the full programs.

## Coffee excursions: from plantation to cup

Unlike an extended coffee-themed tour, **a standalone excursion lets you explore one estate or one aspect of coffee over just a few hours**. The exact itinerary is what matters most. A historic estate, an operating farm, a tasting class and a journey across a coffee-growing region offer distinct experiences.

Our catalog includes visits to coffee plantations, introductions to production and separate tastings. When choosing, compare duration, starting point, guiding language, group size and which services are included.

## Brazil: an excursion to coffee barons' estates

The [Coffee Barons' Estates tour](/brazil/excursion/coffee-baron-estates-tour/) introduces the history of the coffee-growing region of Rio de Janeiro state. Its main experiences involve estate architecture, rural life and the legacy of Brazil's coffee economy.

This excursion lasts **7–8 hours**. According to the published program, transfers, guide services and dinner are included; optional activities cost extra. The precise estates are selected within the agreed itinerary, so a visit to every historical property in the Coffee Valley cannot be promised on a single day.

For travelers interested primarily in history, this is more substantial than a brief tasting. If contemporary bean-processing methods appeal to you, compare it with farm programs in Colombia.

## Pereira: five hours on a farm with tasting

The [Coffee Farm from Pereira excursion](/colombia/pereira/pereira-coffee-farm-tour/) is a standalone **5-hour** visit in Colombia's coffee region. It includes an introduction to assessing aroma, acidity and body, brewing methods and tasting.

The current description specifies an English-language format and hotel departure at 9:00. One important detail: pricing varies with the number of participants, so check the group price and per-person price before booking rather than confusing the two.

Choose this excursion to concentrate on one farm and gain practical experience of coffee without a lengthy interregional itinerary.

## Salento: El Ocaso Farm and the production stages

The [El Ocaso Coffee Farm excursion](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) near [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) covers growing coffee, picking cherries, processing, drying and an introduction to roasting. The program describes viewpoints, tasting freshly brewed coffee and coffee lemonade.

This differs from a trip to historic estates: the main focus is **the actual production cycle**. Check timing and the terms of the particular standalone excursion, rather than assuming every visit to Salento automatically includes El Ocaso.

[Colombia's coffee region](/colombia/place/pereira/) also combines readily with city and nature days. It is best to choose the farm before finalizing the itinerary.

## Panama: a Geisha coffee tasting in the capital

The [Panamanian Geisha Coffee Tasting](/panama/panama-city/geisha-coffee-tasting/) is a separate **1-hour** experience in Panama City. It includes three coffee samples using different processing methods, explanations of their origins, aroma and taste, and paired desserts.

This is **a tasting, not a trip to a highland farm in Boquete**. The venue and language are agreed with the organizers. The format works well during a city or business trip when there are no free days for travel outside the capital.

## Comparing four excursion formats

| Excursion | Main purpose | Format |
|---|---|---|
| [Coffee Barons' Estates](/brazil/excursion/coffee-baron-estates-tour/) | History and rural heritage | 7–8 hours |
| [Pereira coffee farm](/colombia/pereira/pereira-coffee-farm-tour/) | Brewing methods and tasting | 5 hours |
| [El Ocaso](/colombia/salento/el-ocaso-coffee-farm-tour/) | From plant to cup | Farm excursion |
| [Geisha in Panama City](/panama/panama-city/geisha-coffee-tasting/) | Comparing coffee samples | 1 hour |

Do not confuse **an excursion to a historic estate with a demonstration of current production**, or an urban tasting with a walk around a plantation. Each offers a different experience and requires its own amount of time.

## How to choose and book an excursion

Choose the location, then examine the itinerary step by step: farm, harvest, drying, roasting and tasting. Confirm which activities are included in the price, where the excursion begins, what transport is needed and whether guiding is available in your preferred language.

If you want to devote several days to coffee and explore multiple estates, go to the [coffee tours catalog](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/). Ada Tours can help include a chosen standalone excursion in a broader itinerary when the logistics work.

## Frequently asked questions about coffee excursions

### Can I see coffee production and taste different varieties in one day?

Yes, some farm excursions include both experiences. Check the exact list on the selected farm's itinerary.

### Can I visit a farm in Boquete on the one-hour Panama City tasting?

No. The one-hour program is held in the capital and compares coffee samples rather than visiting a plantation.

### Is the coffee barons' estate excursion suitable for a history enthusiast?

Yes. It is a cultural-heritage itinerary through the coffee region, visiting historic estates.
